name: Malimba
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Ntamack, D. 1974. Essai de description phonologique du malimba. Memoire, Univ. de Yaounde.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page mali1280 and its 23 reference records (incl. Ardener 1956; Guthrie 1953; Nurse & Philippson 2003; Bastin, Coupez & Mann 1999; Grollemund et al. 2015; Johnston 1919; Dugast 1949; Koch 1913; Eberhard et al. 2025)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Apart from Ntamack 1974, Jiewo 1988, Nseme 1979, Lamberty 2002/2009 and Ebobissé 2014, the remaining entries are ethnographic/comparative wordlist works or computerised misassignments from the string 'limba' (Sierra Leone Limba; Romanian 'limba').

sources.citation: Lamberty, Melinda. 2002. A Rapid Appraisal Survey of Malimba, ALCAM [610] (Sanaga-Maritime Division, Littoral Province). Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 18 pp. (later issued as SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-004)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic rapid-appraisal survey (dialects, intercomprehension with Duala, vitality, attitudes); no phonology; the two 2000 wordlists in Appendix 2 (pp. 16-18) carry acute tone marks on vowels, but no statement on tone or stress anywhere. Its references list Lobe 1968 (a Mulimba-language book), Nseme 1979, ALCAM 1983.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en: Limba language (Cameroon); fr: Malimba (langue)); Wikidata Q35806; Crossref; Open Library; HAL; theses.fr
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; only classification, speaker numbers and the Lamberty survey are cited. Open Library gives the Ebobissé ISBNs (9783631558225 print; 9783653053982 eBook).

sources.citation: Ebobissé, Carl. 2014 [©2015]. Sawabantu: Eine vergleichende Untersuchung der Küstensprachen Kameruns (Bantu A.20 und A.30). Schriften zur Afrikanistik 24. Frankfurt: Peter Lang. 421 pp. — Kapitel 2 Phonologie (§2.2.4/2.3.4/2.4.4 Toneme, §2.6, §2.7 Silbenstrukturen) and the Mulimba material pp. 395-404

sources.note: The only modern, published description covering Malimba (as 'Mulimba', one of 15 Sawabantu varieties, based on the author's own fieldwork); its tone/toneme sections are the most likely place for a statement on tone vs. stress or accent for Malimba's subgroup.
